steps.title: In the ground
steps.text: The seventeen rare earths always occur together, never alone. The light ones, neodymium among them, come mainly from bastnäsite, mined in hard rock at Bayan Obo in China and Mountain Pass in California, and from monazite, a heavy grain in beach sands. Neodymium is the third most plentiful of them.
steps.india: Monazite in the beach sands of Kerala, Tamil Nadu, Odisha and Andhra Pradesh. It is rich in the light rare earths and poor in the heavy ones.

steps.title: Mine
steps.text: Bastnäsite is mined from open pits, crushed and floated to a concentrate of about 60% rare-earth oxide. Monazite is sorted out of dredged beach sand with magnets and electrostatic plates, alongside ilmenite and zircon.
steps.india: 2,900 tonnes of rare-earth oxide in 2025, 0.7% of the world, all from monazite in beach sands worked by IREL.

steps.title: Crack
steps.text: The concentrate is broken down with hot acid or caustic soda so the rare earths dissolve. Monazite also releases thorium and a little uranium, which are radioactive and must be removed and stored. What is left is a mixed rare-earth chloride or carbonate: all the elements still together.

steps.title: Separate
steps.text: This is the hard part. Neighbouring rare earths behave almost identically, so the solution is run through hundreds of solvent-extraction stages, each shifting the balance slightly, until neodymium comes out on its own as an oxide. China does about 91% of the world's separation.
steps.india: IREL made about 40 tonnes of neodymium in FY25 and targets 500 tonnes in FY27. Toyotsu in Visakhapatnam separates lanthanum, cerium, praseodymium and neodymium.

steps.title: Make
steps.text: The oxide is turned into metal by electrolysis in molten fluoride salt, usually together with praseodymium. The metal is melted with iron and boron, cast into thin flakes, milled to powder, pressed in a magnetic field and sintered into NdFeB magnets. China makes 94% of sintered magnets.
steps.india: A small neodymium-metal plant at Bhopal. A Rs 7,280 crore scheme aims at 6,000 t/yr of magnets.

steps.title: Use
steps.text: NdFeB is the strongest permanent magnet made. It drives the traction motors of electric vehicles, the generators of wind turbines, and the small motors and speakers in electronics.
steps.india: Magnet demand of about 4,000 t/yr, mostly imported.

steps.title: Recycle
steps.text: Grinding dust and offcuts from magnet factories are reprocessed. Magnets in old motors, drives and turbines are rarely recovered yet: they are small, glued in and scattered across many products.
